Named pipes

Source: R/winpipe.R
winpipe.Rd

Functions to create, open, and close named pipes on Windows.

  • winpipe() creates a new named pipe on Windows.

  • is_winpipe() checks if an object is a winpipe.

  • np_listen() blocks the session and listens to a pipe.

  • np_disconnect() disconnects a client.

  • np_exists() checks if a named pipe name exists.

  • np_list() lists all named pipes currently on the machine.

Usage

winpipe(
  name,
  open = "r+",
  server = !np_exists(name),
  blocking = FALSE,
  sddl = sd_default(),
  max_instances = Inf,
  timeout = getOption("timeout")
)

# S3 method for class 'winpipe'
open(con, open = "r+", blocking = FALSE, ...)

is_winpipe(x)

np_listen(con)

np_disconnect(con)

np_exists(name)

np_list()

Arguments

name

[character(1)]

Pipe name, with or without the \\.\pipe\ prefix.

open

[character(1)]

A description of how to open the connection. See pipe.

server

[logical(1)]

Whether the connection should be opened as a server or client. If TRUE, creates the pipe. If FALSE, only connects to it. Defaults to TRUE when no pipe with that can be found, otherwise FALSE.

blocking

[logical(1)]

Whether the connection is blocking. See open. For a server, a blocking open waits until a client connects (see timeout). A non-blocking open returns immediately and np_listen() can accept a client later. For reads, a blocking connection waits for data, while a non-blocking one returns only what is available (possibly nothing) and leaves a partial line for the next read. Writes always block. Defaults to FALSE.

sddl

[winpipe_sd] or [character(1)]

Security descriptor string, or a security descriptor built with sd_create. Ignored if server is FALSE. Defaults to the default DACL of the current token (sd_default).

max_instances

[numeric(1)]

Maximum allowed instances that can be opened on a named pipe. Can be a number between 1 and 254. If Inf, a maximum of 255 instances is allowed. max_instances is set on the creation of the pipe. This means that all connections connecting to an existing pipe cannot change the maximum number of instances. Defaults to Inf.

timeout

[numeric(1)]

Seconds without progress before a read, write, accept, or open fails with an error. If Inf, waits forever. Defaults to getOption("timeout"). A read that times out after receiving bytes returns them with a warning instead of discarding them.

con

[winpipe]

A winpipe connection created by winpipe.

...

Further arguments passed to open.

x

Any object.

Value

named_pipe returns a connection of class "named_pipe". All methods accepting a connection work on named pipes. Use open = "r+b" for readBin and writeBin.

Details

Named pipes behave differently depending on whether they are initialized as a server or client. When server = TRUE, open() creates the named pipe so that a client can connect to it. With blocking = TRUE the open waits for a client to connect; otherwise run np_listen() to block the session until one does. np_disconnect() drops the current client and discards all unread data. close() destroys the instance but does not disconnect first, so data already written stays readable by the client.

When server = FALSE, the named pipe cannot be created or destroyed. Clients can only read or write but not change the state of the named pipe. If a client named pipe is opened but there is no server instance available to answer it, it will block the session until its timeout is reached or an interrupt is signaled.

Blocking

The principles of blocking are explained in pipe. Since readLines() with n = -1 reads until the end of the input, reading all lines from a server blocks the session until the client signals the end of the input by closing the connection.

Examples

server <- winpipe("test")
client <- winpipe("test", server = FALSE)

# Nothing written yet
readLines(server)
#> character(0)

# Client writes to pipe
cat("hello\n", file = client)
writeLines("world", client)

# Server can now receive the content
readLines(server)
#> [1] "hello" "world"

close(client)
close(server)

# To read binary, you need to specify it
server <- winpipe("test")
try(writeBin(raw(1), server))
#> Error in writeBin(raw(1), server) : can only write to a binary connection
close(server)

server <- winpipe("test", open = "r+b")
client <- winpipe("test", open = "r+b", server = FALSE)
writeBin(as.raw(1), server)
readBin(client, "raw")
#> [1] 01

close(server)
close(client)
